/** First and last migrations whose private functions these lists classify. */
export const SERVING_FUNCTION_PRIVILEGE_MIGRATIONS = { first: 247, last: 265 } as const;

/**
 * SELECT-only facts from the executing connection, including inherited access.
 * $1 is the schema, $2 the signatures and $3 whether each must be executable.
 */
export const SERVING_FUNCTION_PRIVILEGES_SQL = `SELECT
  current_user::text AS runtime_role, required.signature, required.expected_execute,
  COALESCE(has_schema_privilege(current_user, n.oid, 'USAGE'), FALSE) AS schema_usage,
  p.oid IS NOT NULL AS function_exists,
  COALESCE(p.pronamespace = anchor.relnamespace AND p.proowner = anchor.relowner, FALSE) AS anchored_owner,
  COALESCE(p.prosecdef, FALSE) AS security_definer,
  COALESCE(p.proconfig = ARRAY['search_path=pg_catalog, ' || quote_ident(n.nspname) || ', pg_temp'], FALSE) AS pinned_search_path,
  COALESCE(pg_has_role(current_user, p.proowner, 'USAGE'), FALSE) AS owner_equivalent,
  COALESCE(has_function_privilege(current_user, p.oid, 'EXECUTE'), FALSE) AS can_execute
FROM unnest($2::text[], $3::boolean[]) AS required(signature, expected_execute)
LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.nspname = $1
LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class anchor ON anchor.relnamespace = n.oid AND anchor.relname = 'participation_owners'
LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_proc p
  ON p.oid = pg_catalog.to_regprocedure(quote_ident(n.nspname) || '.' || required.signature)`;

export function servingFunctionPrivilegeParameters(schema: string) {
  const grants = SERVING_FUNCTION_EXECUTE_GRANTS.map((grant) => grant.signature);
  return [
    schema,
    [...grants, ...SERVING_FUNCTION_EXECUTE_DENIALS],
    [...grants.map(() => true), ...SERVING_FUNCTION_EXECUTE_DENIALS.map(() => false)],
  ] as const;
}

export class ServingFunctionPrivilegesRefused extends Error {
  constructor(readonly failures: readonly string[]) {
    super("Serving-role function privileges refused");
  }
}

/** Returns the serving role; failures name signatures and facts, never values. */
export function assertServingFunctionPrivileges(rows: readonly Record<string, unknown>[]): string {
  const expected = SERVING_FUNCTION_EXECUTE_GRANTS.length + SERVING_FUNCTION_EXECUTE_DENIALS.length;
  const role = rows[0]?.runtime_role;
  if (rows.length !== expected || typeof role !== "string" || role.length === 0)
    throw new ServingFunctionPrivilegesRefused(["privilege facts incomplete"]);
  const failures: string[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<unknown>();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const signature = String(row.signature);
    if (row.runtime_role !== role || seen.has(row.signature))
      failures.push(`${signature}: facts differ`);
    seen.add(row.signature);
    if (row.schema_usage !== true) failures.push(`${signature}: schema usage missing`);
    if (row.function_exists !== true) failures.push(`${signature}: function missing`);
    if (row.anchored_owner !== true) failures.push(`${signature}: schema or owner differs`);
    // A granted entry point runs as the owner with a fixed search_path. Denied
    // helpers and triggers keep whatever shape their migration gave them.
    if (row.expected_execute === true && row.security_definer !== true)
      failures.push(`${signature}: not security definer`);
    if (row.expected_execute === true && row.pinned_search_path !== true)
      failures.push(`${signature}: search_path not pinned`);
    if (row.owner_equivalent !== false)
      failures.push(`${signature}: serving role is owner-equivalent`);
    if (row.can_execute !== row.expected_execute)
      failures.push(
        `${signature}: ${row.expected_execute === true ? "EXECUTE missing" : "EXECUTE must be denied"}`,
      );
  }
  if (failures.length > 0) throw new ServingFunctionPrivilegesRefused(failures);
  return role;
}

review.body:
Independent source review of exact head 4a20cc598a9371536ad2dddbbd4269cc6a82c2fb.

One blocking finding remains in packages/platform-cf/src/serving-function-privileges.ts, SERVING_FUNCTION_PRIVILEGES_SQL: owner_equivalent checks only pg_has_role(current_user, p.proowner, 'USAGE'). A serving role with an owner membership granted WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE returns false for USAGE and has no immediate access to the 147 denied functions, so the current preflight accepts all 170 facts. That role can then SET ROLE to the owner and execute every denied function.

I reproduced this with the exact fetched SQL and assertServingFunctionPrivileges on a disposable, isolated postgres:17.11 catalog fixture containing all 170 reviewed signatures, correct ownership and search paths, and exactly the 23 proposed EXECUTE grants. Result: preflight accepted g1_review_app; immediate owner USAGE=false; owner SET=true; after SET ROLE, 147/147 denials were executable. This is a source admission failure, not a claim that staging currently has that membership. PostgreSQL 17 distinguishes USAGE from SET explicitly: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions-info.html#FUNCTIONS-INFO-ACCESS-TABLE .

Please reject both inherited owner access and the ability to SET ROLE to the owner, including indirect memberships, and add a native PostgreSQL regression for a NOINHERIT serving role with SET-enabled owner membership. Keep the ordinary limited role admitted. This repair does not require changing the proposed 23 grants or any managed role.

The rest of the reviewed source is satisfactory: the new account-bound cancellation validates the exact account/session/attempt/artifact/capture and serializes with claim, only closing registered uploads. The broad closure and legacy/guest helpers stay denied. The grant block contains exactly 23 signatures, matches the shared list, and is disjoint from the 147 denials. I independently recomputed migration 0265 SHA256 337b5469bdf01595413349517f1c0750530280a4a38ac8fd007a2d2e3c4e106f, body pin ae7c0121308ecf6b544682d5ba0d7aba89db91eb68bb1e805c2faa960a2964e4, and the 265-entry ledger; the prior 264 manifest entries are unchanged. The trimmed SQL between the ordinary-account grant markers hashes to 474d70e56baef8874150f509c40207957affc10682934270c49e9d784604f814.

All 13 hosted checks pass on this exact head. I did not rerun the full product suites locally; the two independent reproductions used fetched source modules and an isolated catalog fixture. A passing URL preflight still needs a fresh operator receipt binding that connection to the effective staging Hyperdrive origin and serving principal.

Source clearance is pending the owner-equivalence repair and exact-successor CI. Actual staging grant application remains a separate, explicit permission change; no migration, grant, credential or deployment was performed by this review.

direction.body:
Independent review checkpoint and continuation direction.

I reviewed api-next#605 at 4a20cc598a9371536ad2dddbbd4269cc6a82c2fb and verified all 13 hosted checks are green. The narrow cancellation boundary and the exact 23-function grant block are sound, but the preflight has one source blocker: its owner-equivalence check uses USAGE only. An owner membership with INHERIT FALSE and SET TRUE passes the exact SQL/assertion, then SET ROLE makes all 147 denied functions executable. I reproduced that on an isolated local PostgreSQL 17.11 catalog fixture. The exact-head review is https://github.com/pirate-social-club/api-next/pull/605#pullrequestreview-5507108723 . Please reject both inherited owner access and SET-enabled owner access, cover indirect memberships in the native regression, publish the successor and obtain exact-head CI. No staging role change is needed to implement or test this repair.

G3 has a separate blocking regression. I fetched bd319b438e6e8ef92235050fb6475f957efe110b and confirmed its tree is the pre-#64 tree plus #65's test line. That also restores the old equality-only privacy classifier for the existing /telegram/link, /telegram/link/callback and /telegram/link/account routes. With the pinned @solidjs/router 2.0.0-next.16, all 18 tested spellings route; 15 aliases bypass the reverted private classification and retain synthetic callback query values in the request passed to the SSR conditional. /TELEGRAM/LINK/CALLBACK/ and /%74elegram/link/callback are two concrete examples. Current corrected privacy source refuses those aliases and scrubs them. This was an exact-module/control-flow reproduction, not a deployed SSR run or a real credential leak.

Do not use bd319b43 as the Part A recovery candidate. Prepare a successor on the exclusively owned Solid branch that removes the probe while preserving the shared router-equivalent private classification, alias refusal, callback scrubbing, private response/error headers and regressions for the existing linking routes. Preserve #65 and unrelated main changes. Publish it normally, run the appropriate checks/build/fingerprint and send the exact source back for independent review. Tree equality to the vulnerable pre-#64 source is not an acceptance criterion. Preparing and reviewing this source repair is already authorized; it needs no new product-owner decision. Retain the held candidate as historical evidence and update the live packet explicitly.

G2 remains in Part B, with matched API/media source and fresh bindings. Treat the packet's claim that every existing instance reaching alignment after deploy uses the new producer as unverified until actual Workflow version/step binding is established. Counts alone do not prove that binding.
